purpose: Classify source authority, temporal validity, accessibility, completeness and freshness so the system can determine whether a source is suitable for current law, historical law, official procedure, property evidence or supporting context.
use_rules: Primary legislation is used for statutory propositions within its applicable temporal and jurisdictional scope.
A statutory instrument is checked against its enabling framework and commencement/effective provisions.
Case law is linked to the proposition actually decided or reasoned and its temporal authority.
Official guidance explains procedure or administration and does not silently override legislation.
Official property records are evidence of the record state within their scope; they do not automatically prove matters outside that scope.
Secondary sources may aid discovery and explanation but do not replace required primary or official evidence.
A source can be historically valid while no longer being current.
A source can be current but incomplete for the specific proposition being answered.
hard_stops: Never call a source current without checking its temporal status.
Never treat a superseded source as current law.
Never treat an inaccessible or incomplete source as if its missing content were verified.
Never use a secondary source to replace required authoritative evidence.
Never infer historical validity solely from a current consolidated webpage.
Never allow freshness to override source authority.
